content.json:
# Azure Arc Connected Servers - Multicloud and Hybrid Inventory
Inventory Azure Arc-enabled servers across AWS, GCP, other clouds, and on-premises environments. The server lists query `Microsoft.HybridCompute/machines` directly and do not require a Defender for Servers plan or a Defender for Cloud security connector.

**Scope:** All server lists use the selected Azure subscriptions and your resource read permissions. AWS account and GCP project filters apply only to the Defender for Cloud discovery tables. Connection status is shown as reported by Azure Arc; an Arc resource can exist even when its agent is disconnected.

**Environment:** AWS and GCP are identified by `properties.cloudMetadata.provider`, not by the resource's Azure location, its name, or the environment label in Defender for Cloud inventory. Other providers and servers with missing provider metadata appear under **Other cloud / on-premises** as well as **All Arc servers**. Unknown metadata does not prove that a server is on-premises.

parameters.name: Subscriptions
parameters.description: Select the Azure subscriptions to search for Arc resources and Defender for Cloud discovery records.

parameters.name: AWSSecurityConnectors
parameters.label: AWS account (discovery only)
parameters.description: Filter Defender for Cloud EC2 discovery records by security connector. This does not filter the Azure Arc server inventory.
parameters.query:
Resources
| where type =~ 'microsoft.security/securityconnectors'
| where tostring(properties.environmentName) =~ 'aws'
| project value = tolower(id), label = strcat(tostring(properties.hierarchyIdentifier), ' (', name, ')')
| order by label asc

parameters.name: GCPSecuityConnectors
parameters.label: GCP project (discovery only)
parameters.description: Filter Defender for Cloud GCP compute discovery records by security connector. This does not filter the Azure Arc server inventory.
parameters.query:
Resources
| where type =~ 'microsoft.security/securityconnectors'
| where tostring(properties.environmentName) =~ 'gcp'
| project value = tolower(id), label = strcat(tostring(properties.hierarchyIdentifier), ' (', name, ')')
| order by label asc

content.json:
## All Azure Arc-enabled servers
Every Arc server resource visible in the selected subscriptions is included, even without Defender for Cloud discovery records or cloud-provider metadata. Use **ConnectionStatus** to distinguish currently connected agents from disconnected or other states.

content.query:
Resources
| where type =~ 'microsoft.hybridcompute/machines'
| extend provider = tolower(trim(' ', tostring(properties.cloudMetadata.provider)))
| extend environment = case(provider == 'aws', 'AWS', provider == 'gcp', 'GCP', 'Other cloud / on-premises')
| project Server = name, ComputerName = coalesce(tostring(properties.osProfile.computerName), tostring(properties.machineFqdn), name), Environment = environment, CloudProvider = iff(isempty(provider), 'Unknown', tostring(properties.cloudMetadata.provider)), ConnectionStatus = coalesce(tostring(properties.status), 'Unknown'), OSName = coalesce(tostring(properties.osName), tostring(properties.osType), 'Unknown'), AgentVersion = tostring(properties.agentVersion), SubscriptionId = subscriptionId, ResourceGroup = resourceGroup, Location = location, ResourceId = id
| order by Server asc
content.noDataMessage: No Azure Arc-enabled servers were found in the selected subscriptions. Check the subscription selection and your resource read permissions, or onboard servers to Azure Arc.

content.json:
## Azure Arc-enabled servers in AWS
These Arc resources report AWS in their cloud-provider metadata. The AWS account selector does not filter this list. Servers with unknown provider metadata remain visible in **All Arc servers** and **Other cloud / on-premises**.

content.query:
Resources
| where type =~ 'microsoft.hybridcompute/machines'
| extend provider = tolower(trim(' ', tostring(properties.cloudMetadata.provider)))
| where provider == 'aws'
| project Server = name, ComputerName = coalesce(tostring(properties.osProfile.computerName), tostring(properties.machineFqdn), name), CloudProvider = tostring(properties.cloudMetadata.provider), ConnectionStatus = coalesce(tostring(properties.status), 'Unknown'), OSName = coalesce(tostring(properties.osName), tostring(properties.osType), 'Unknown'), AgentVersion = tostring(properties.agentVersion), SubscriptionId = subscriptionId, ResourceGroup = resourceGroup, Location = location, ResourceId = id
| order by Server asc
content.noDataMessage: No Azure Arc-enabled servers reporting AWS as their cloud provider were found in the selected subscriptions. Check All Arc servers and Other cloud / on-premises for servers with unknown or different provider metadata.

content.json:
## EC2 instances discovered by Defender for Cloud
This separate discovery list uses the selected AWS security connectors. **ArcMatch** is a name-based hint, not proof of installation or absence: names can differ or be reused across accounts and regions, Arc resources can be in another subscription, and discovery records can lag. A possible match checks the Arc resource name, computer name, and FQDN within the same subscription; verify **PossibleArcResources** against the native instance identity. Do not treat an unmatched record as definitely without Arc.

content.query:
SecurityResources
| where type =~ 'microsoft.security/assessments'
| extend resourceDetails = properties.resourceDetails, additionalData = properties.additionalData
| where tostring(resourceDetails.Source) =~ 'aws'
| where tostring(resourceDetails.ResourceType) =~ 'microsoft.security/securityconnectors/ec2instance'
| extend resourceId = tolower(coalesce(tostring(resourceDetails.Id), tostring(resourceDetails.AzureResourceId), extract('(?i)^(.+)/providers/microsoft.security/assessments/[^/]+$', 1, id))), nativeResourceId = tostring(resourceDetails.NativeResourceId)
| extend securityConnectorId = tolower(coalesce(tostring(resourceDetails.ConnectorId), extract('(?i)^(.+/providers/microsoft.security/securityconnectors/[^/]+)', 1, resourceId)))
| where '*' in ({AWSSecurityConnectors}) or securityConnectorId in~ ({AWSSecurityConnectors})
| extend resourceName = coalesce(tostring(additionalData.ResourceName), tostring(resourceDetails.ResourceName), extract('([^/]+)$', 1, nativeResourceId), extract('([^/]+)$', 1, resourceId))
| summarize resourceName = max(resourceName), nativeResourceId = max(nativeResourceId), securityConnectorId = max(securityConnectorId) by resourceId, subscriptionId
| extend matchName = tolower(resourceName), subscriptionKey = tolower(subscriptionId)
| join kind=leftouter (
    Resources
    | where type =~ 'microsoft.hybridcompute/machines'
    | extend provider = tolower(trim(' ', tostring(properties.cloudMetadata.provider)))
    | where provider == 'aws' or isempty(provider)
    | extend matchNames = pack_array(tolower(name), tolower(tostring(properties.osProfile.computerName)), tolower(tostring(properties.machineFqdn)))
    | mv-expand matchName = matchNames
    | extend matchName = tostring(matchName), subscriptionKey = tolower(subscriptionId)
    | where isnotempty(matchName)
    | summarize possibleArcResources = make_set(id) by matchName, subscriptionKey
) on matchName, subscriptionKey
| extend ArcMatch = iff(isempty(tostring(possibleArcResources)), 'Not verified - no name match in scope', 'Possible name match only - verify resource identity')
| project ResourceName = resourceName, NativeResourceId = nativeResourceId, ArcMatch, PossibleArcResources = possibleArcResources, SubscriptionId = subscriptionId, ResourceGroup = tostring(split(resourceId, '/')[4]), ConnectorId = securityConnectorId, ResourceId = resourceId
| order by ResourceName asc
content.noDataMessage: No AWS EC2 discovery records were found for the selected subscriptions and AWS security connectors. This does not prove that AWS has no instances. Check connector configuration, permissions, and discovery freshness; Arc resources are listed independently above.

## GCP virtual machines discovered by Defender for Cloud
This separate discovery list uses the selected GCP security connectors. **ArcMatch** is a name-based hint, not proof of installation or absence: names can differ or be reused across projects and zones, Arc resources can be in another subscription, and discovery records can lag. A possible match checks the Arc resource name, computer name, and FQDN within the same subscription; verify **PossibleArcResources** against the native instance identity. Do not treat an unmatched record as definitely without Arc.

content.query:
SecurityResources
| where type =~ 'microsoft.security/assessments'
| extend resourceDetails = properties.resourceDetails, additionalData = properties.additionalData
| where tostring(resourceDetails.Source) =~ 'gcp'
| where tostring(resourceDetails.ResourceType) =~ 'microsoft.security/securityconnectors/computeinstances'
| extend resourceId = tolower(coalesce(tostring(resourceDetails.Id), tostring(resourceDetails.AzureResourceId), extract('(?i)^(.+)/providers/microsoft.security/assessments/[^/]+$', 1, id))), nativeResourceId = tostring(resourceDetails.NativeResourceId)
| extend securityConnectorId = tolower(coalesce(tostring(resourceDetails.ConnectorId), extract('(?i)^(.+/providers/microsoft.security/securityconnectors/[^/]+)', 1, resourceId)))
| where '*' in ({GCPSecuityConnectors}) or securityConnectorId in~ ({GCPSecuityConnectors})
| extend resourceName = coalesce(tostring(additionalData.ResourceName), tostring(resourceDetails.ResourceName), extract('([^/]+)$', 1, nativeResourceId), extract('([^/]+)$', 1, resourceId))
| summarize resourceName = max(resourceName), nativeResourceId = max(nativeResourceId), securityConnectorId = max(securityConnectorId) by resourceId, subscriptionId
| extend matchName = tolower(resourceName), subscriptionKey = tolower(subscriptionId)
| join kind=leftouter (

    | where type =~ 'microsoft.hybridcompute/machines'
    | extend provider = tolower(trim(' ', tostring(properties.cloudMetadata.provider)))
    | where provider == 'gcp' or isempty(provider)
    | extend matchNames = pack_array(tolower(name), tolower(tostring(properties.osProfile.computerName)), tolower(tostring(properties.machineFqdn)))

| project ResourceName = resourceName, NativeResourceId = nativeResourceId, ArcMatch, PossibleArcResources = possibleArcResources, SubscriptionId = subscriptionId, ResourceGroup = tostring(split(resourceId, '/')[4]), ConnectorId = securityConnectorId, ResourceId = resourceId
| order by ResourceName asc

content.json:
## Azure Arc-enabled servers in other clouds and on-premises
Includes private clouds, datacenters, edge locations, other reported providers, and servers without cloud-provider metadata. **CloudProvider = Unknown** means the hosting environment cannot be determined from the Arc resource; it is not an assertion that the server is on-premises. Azure Arc resources can be labeled **Azure** in Defender for Cloud inventory because they are represented as Azure resources, regardless of where the server runs.

content.query:
Resources
| where type =~ 'microsoft.hybridcompute/machines'
| extend provider = tolower(trim(' ', tostring(properties.cloudMetadata.provider)))
| where provider !in ('aws', 'gcp')
| project Server = name, ComputerName = coalesce(tostring(properties.osProfile.computerName), tostring(properties.machineFqdn), name), CloudProvider = iff(isempty(provider), 'Unknown', tostring(properties.cloudMetadata.provider)), ConnectionStatus = coalesce(tostring(properties.status), 'Unknown'), OSName = coalesce(tostring(properties.osName), tostring(properties.osType), 'Unknown'), AgentVersion = tostring(properties.agentVersion), SubscriptionId = subscriptionId, ResourceGroup = resourceGroup, Location = location, ResourceId = id
| order by Server asc
content.noDataMessage: No Azure Arc-enabled servers with other or unknown cloud-provider metadata were found in the selected subscriptions. Check the AWS, GCP, or All Arc servers tabs, and verify your subscription selection and resource read permissions.
